newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Soccer star Maradona may be questioned in drug case.
newsitem.headline: Soccer star Maradona may be questioned in drug case.

text.p: Former Argentine soccer star Diego Maradona and his manager Guillermo Coppola may be questioned by an Argentine judge after relatives of both were arrested on drug-possession charges in dawn raids on Friday.

"If necessary I will summon Maradona and Coppola," Judge Hernan Bernasconi told reporters, after a Buenos Aires police police drugs squad arrested Maradona's brother-in-law Gabriel Esposito, Coppola's cousin Claudio Coppola and two others.
The judge said he had serious evidence that three of those held "are implicated in drug peddling ... which carries prison terms of four to 15 years."

"I don't want to talk about anyone's relatives and I want to make it clear that nobody is being charged with any crime just because of the fact they have a more or less famous surname," said Bernasconi.

The arrests come just a week after Argentine magazine Noticias reported in a cover story that Maradona, 35, who admits he is addicted to drugs, has burnt out his brain's frontal lobes by cocaine sniffing and is in danger of dropping dead.

Claiming to have had access to a brain scan and medical tests, Noticias diagnosed "cell death in the frontal lobe with loss of blood circulation" and said Maradona "cannot control his aggression, or detect people standing behind him."

The captain of the 1986 World Cup winning team, who played for Buenos Aires team Boca Juniors since last year but whose future there is uncertain, made the headlines again in August when he was treated at a Swiss drug rehabilitation centre.
He became enraged after getting stuck in an elevator and smashed up furniture at a Spanish hotel.

Maradona is at the centre of allegations by local weightlifter Sergio Parodi, who says Maradona's urine sample was switched with another player's in a post-match drugs test last August. Maradona's test was clean but the other player, who had no drugs history, tested positive and has been suspended.
Maradona is also suing a handful of former colleagues and acquaintances for comments made to British journalist Jimmy Burns in his unauthorised biography, "The Hand of God."
Once the most expensive player in the world, Maradona's career has since been ridden with scandal.

In 1994 he was temporarily banned from international matches after failing a dope test at the World Cup finals in the United States. In a stressful moment a few months earlier, he opened fired with an air rifle on Argentine reporters.
